target.title: refactor: use built-in glob for package manifests
target.body:
AI-assisted change. Maintainer-requested dependency cleanup.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw carried `glob` as a direct production dependency for one package-manifest resource expansion, even though the supported Node floor provides stable filesystem globbing with the required behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use `node:fs` `globSync` for manifest resource discovery and resolve its relative matches against the package root. A focused regression test covers directory matches and the existing hidden-path exclusion; the direct dependency and generated lock artifacts are removed.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. The published npm dependency tree drops `glob` and `path-scurry`, and the root manifest has one fewer direct dependency.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/agents/sessions/package-manager.test.ts`: 1 file passed, 6 tests passed on Linux/Node.
- `node scripts/generate-npm-shrinkwrap.mjs --check`: root shrinkwrap current.
- `node scripts/check-dependency-pins.mjs`: 504 direct specs checked, 0 violations.
- `pnpm build`: passed, including runtime, plugin SDK declaration, and Control UI build phases.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main`: clean; no accepted/actionable findings.
- `pnpm check:changed` was attempted on the rebased tree, but current `main` fails its repository-wide TypeScript LOC ratchet before the remaining lanes; the reported files are unrelated to this five-file diff.
